acceptance: Cleanup emits a nonzero analysis-complete progress update before the first potentially long AI request.
Each primary and verifier request reports a distinct, monotonic progress step with batch and pass information.
AI progress is mapped into a bounded operation phase and never reports 100 percent before deterministic validation and rendering finish.
Cleanup without eligible AI questions still advances monotonically through validation/rendering and completes at 100 percent.
The existing five-argument UI progress callback remains compatible, cancellation and token accounting remain unchanged, and focused tests pass.
No source cleanup semantics, AI prompts, batch sizing, runtime project data, commits, push, or PR are changed.
alignment.reason: The defect is isolated to progress plumbing and messages; completion percentage can be derived deterministically from known batches and their primary/verifier calls without changing cleanup results.
scope: In scope: Cleanup V2 progress callback contracts, progress phase mapping, localized-neutral operator messages, focused automated tests, requirement/spec and Text Cleanup component documentation. Out of scope: changing cleanup decisions/prompts/batch sizing, adding fake timer progress, modifying runtime project D:\TEMP\Carrier, migrating legacy data, repairing unrelated historical requirement links, commits, push, PR, or live LM Studio automation.
alignment.source: Chat 2026-07-27: user observed Cleanup In Progress remaining at 0% while LM Studio was actively processing AI adjudication, then asked to fix bugs after the run completed
alignment.understanding: Cleanup V2 performs deterministic analysis and many bounded primary/verifier AI calls, but its orchestration suppresses adjudication progress and emits a hard-coded zero percent. The fix will propagate per-request adjudication progress through an adapter into the existing UI callback, map phases monotonically across the operation, and preserve cancellation, token accounting, provider fallback, and cleanup output semantics.

evidence.summary: Focused progress checks fail on baseline: adjudication emits only one batch event, orchestration passes no AI callback, and every UI percent is zero.
Cleanup orchestration supplies progress_callback=None to AI adjudication, so the global progress test fails before any mapped AI update.
Cleanup without AI emits only zero percentages and therefore fails to report phase completion.
AI adjudication reports primary, verifier, and verified work-unit updates; focused check passes.
Cleanup maps AI work units to monotonic global percentages and reserves 100 percent for completion.
Cleanup without AI advances through real phases and completes at 100 percent.

intent.statement: Text Cleanup progress dialog remains at 0 percent during AI adjudication even while local-model primary and verifier requests are running

examples: For 54 batches, request phases identify Batch 12/54 Primary and Batch 12/54 Verifier within 108 total calls.
spec_items.statement: AI adjudication reports primary and verifier request phases with completed-work and total-work counts for every batch.
spec_items.threshold: Every emitted completed-work count is within 0..total and never decreases.

examples: Analysis reaches 5%, AI calls occupy 5..90%, validation/rendering occupy 90..99%, and successful persistence emits 100%.
spec_items.statement: Cleanup maps analysis, AI adjudication, validation, rendering, and persistence into monotonic UI percentages while emitting 100 only after successful completion.
spec_items.threshold: All percentages are integers in 0..100, monotonically nondecreasing, and no pre-completion update equals 100.
